initial_scene: The humanoid faces the camera behind a tabletop. A red-cased multimeter stands on a black square to the image left of an empty open gray basket. Its anatomical right hand is free beside the meter; its anatomical left hand is at the basket far rim.

observed_sequence.action: Initial hold with both hands low; the meter remains upright on the tabletop and the basket is empty.
The anatomical right arm extends toward the red meter and positions the articulated hand around it. The left hand remains by the basket far rim.

The right fingers grasp the meter and turn it from its upright support pose toward a roughly horizontal orientation, drawing it off the tabletop. Native frames 176 and 200 show grasp/contact; frame 222 shows the meter tipped and being raised.
The right hand raises the grasped meter clear of the tabletop and carries it inward toward the basket. Frame 256 shows a clear air gap under the meter.
The right hand brings the meter over the basket opening and rotates it toward a more upright orientation. The left hand shifts slightly along the far rim without receiving the meter.
The right hand opens and releases the meter above the basket interior. Native frame 366 shows the meter falling freely below the open hand inside the basket.
The meter rocks/tumbles against the basket interior and settles nearly flat near its nearer wall; the right hand lifts away.
The right arm withdraws to a low position beside the torso. The red meter remains inside the basket and the left hand remains at its far rim.
